# Parent-drift breadcrumb comment (echo-safe, nearest-represented-ancestor)

## Context / Problem

When a local parent cannot be represented in Jira — the parent is a non-epic and this
project permits only Epic parents — the outbound differ already **suppresses the parent
field** (`adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py`: `parent_id in local_ticket_types` and a
non-epic `parent_type` ⇒ the parent diff is dropped). The child then lands as an
under-defined leaf with no hint its defining context lives elsewhere. Alt-link self-heal
was rejected as echo-unsafe. We need an echo-safe breadcrumb comment pointing the Jira
user at the nearest ancestor that *is* visible in Jira, never re-ingested inbound.

## Approach

Emit the breadcrumb from the **outbound comment differ**, not the apply-time scalar
recorder `pass_io.record_parent_divergence` (see Scope). Integrate into
`outbound_comments._diff_comments`, which already (a) resolves the child's Jira comment
list (snapshot, or one bounded `client.get_comments` live fetch), (b) builds the
marker-stripped `jira_bodies` dedup set, (c) holds `binding_store`. The pure cluster
`_breadcrumb_target` + `_build_parent_breadcrumb` lives in `parent_breadcrumb.py` (split
for the 800-line cap; `outbound_comments` re-exports the names).

On a child whose direct parent is type-collapsed, walk upward via `local_parents` and name
the **nearest ancestor with a bound Jira key** (`binding_store.get_jira_key`). The body is
decorated with `RECONCILER_MARKER` and returned as an ordinary `{"action":"add",...}`
mutation, posted through the existing `client.add_comment` path.

**Echo-safety.** Inbound echo-safety comes solely from the `RECONCILER_MARKER` substring
check in `inbound_collection_diffs._diff_comments_inbound` (`if RECONCILER_MARKER in
body_text: continue`). It is NOT `_is_machine_marker_comment` (an *outbound* exclusion that
matches only `_EXCLUDED_COMMENT_PREFIXES`, which the body does not start with).
`_normalize_comment_body` strips `RECONCILER_MARKER`, so the marker never enters the dedup
key — it serves only inbound suppression.

**Append-once.** Dedup on a **stable identity tag** `<!-- rebar:parent-breadcrumb -->`
(`PARENT_BREADCRUMB_TAG`), NOT the variable ancestor key: scan the resolved comments for
the tag; if present, emit nothing (first-writer-wins, stable across passes even if the
nearest represented ancestor later changes). `_normalize_comment_body` does not strip this
tag. The outbound comment path is ADD-only, so the original is intentionally not rewritten
(accepted limitation). Adds no transport capability; cannot loop.

## Scope

- `parent_breadcrumb.py` (new) — pure `_breadcrumb_target` (precondition + nearest-bound
  ancestor walk) and `_build_parent_breadcrumb` (0-or-1 decorated `"add"` mutation).
- `outbound_comments.py` — integrate `_build_parent_breadcrumb` into `_diff_comments`; new
  params `local_parents` (`{id->parent_id}`) and `local_ticket_types`, both defaulting to
  `None` (no breadcrumb when absent — every existing caller/test unchanged); re-export the
  cluster names.
- `outbound_mutation_builders.py` — thread `local_parents`/`local_ticket_types` into the
  `_diff_comments` call.
- `outbound_differ.py` — build `local_parents` `{ticket_id -> parent_id}` beside the
  existing `local_ticket_types` build and thread it down.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_parent_breadcrumb.py` (new).

**Out of scope (with reason):** `pass_io.record_parent_divergence` and its call sites
(`dispatch_one.py`, `acli_cli_ops.py`) are NOT touched — its signature
`(kind, key, local_id, parent, exc, repo_root)` is scalar-only (`parent` is the *failed*
key/CLEAR sentinel) with no ticket graph, binding store, comment client, or snapshot;
`acli_cli_ops.py` passes `local_id=None` (transport boundary). The differ seam detects the
same drift class earlier with all inputs present. **CREATE path** is untouched: the
breadcrumb needs the child's Jira issue to exist, so it follows on the next (bound) pass.

## Body content contract

Deterministic (no timestamps, so dedup is stable). Nearest ancestor `PROJ-42`:

```
This ticket's parent hierarchy could not be fully represented in Jira. Nearest tracked ancestor: PROJ-42. Full parent context is maintained in rebar.
<!-- rebar:parent-breadcrumb -->
```
(plus the appended `RECONCILER_MARKER`.) If ≥1 intervening ancestor was skipped for
lacking a bound key, `One or more intervening parent levels are not represented in Jira.`
is inserted before the last sentence.

## Drift-condition parity (blank/untyped parent)

The breadcrumb gate and the outbound_fields suppression fire on the **same** children —
no parent-type class is suppressed outbound yet left without a breadcrumb.
`local_ticket_types` is built as `{ticket_id: t.get("ticket_type", "")}` — the value
defaults to `""`, **never `None`** for a present key. So: a **present non-epic parent**
(including blank `""`) is both suppressed and breadcrumbed; a **present `"epic"` parent**
triggers neither; a **parent absent** from the map triggers neither (suppression needs
`parent_id in local_ticket_types`; the gate's `parent_type is None` branch skips). The
`parent_type is None` branch therefore excludes only the parent-absent case, exactly what
suppression also excludes — intended parity, not an untested gap.

## Portability

In-process differ logic plus the existing `TicketTransport` comment port
(`add_comment`/`get_comments`), implemented by both backends. No CI-system dependency, new
binary, filesystem assumption, or transport capability; runs identically across
library/CLI/MCP and both Jira deployments. With the ancestor maps absent it is a no-op.

## Testing

In-process unit tests over `_build_parent_breadcrumb`/`_breadcrumb_target` (stub binding
store, synthetic snapshots; pure logic).

## Accepted limitation

No supersede/edit of a stale breadcrumb: the path is ADD-only, so a changed nearest
ancestor leaves the original in place — still a valid "context lives upward, see rebar"
pointer, preferred over conflicting duplicates.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A bound child with a type-collapsed, bound parent appends exactly one breadcrumb
  naming the nearest represented ancestor's Jira key and carrying both the
  `<!-- rebar:parent-breadcrumb -->` tag and `RECONCILER_MARKER` — verified by
  `test_parent_breadcrumb.py::test_breadcrumb_emitted`.
- [x] Append-once via the stable tag, including when the nearest represented ancestor
  changes across passes (no conflicting second comment) — verified by
  `test_parent_breadcrumb.py::test_breadcrumb_idempotent_across_ancestor_change`.
- [x] When the walk skips an unbound intervening ancestor to reach a bound one, the body
  names the bound ancestor and states the intervening levels are not represented —
  verified by `test_parent_breadcrumb.py::test_unrepresented_intervening_ancestor_noted`.
- [x] No ancestor with a bound Jira key ⇒ no breadcrumb — verified by
  `test_parent_breadcrumb.py::test_breadcrumb_omitted_when_no_bound_ancestor`.
- [x] The breadcrumb body is suppressed inbound by `_diff_comments_inbound` (carries
  `RECONCILER_MARKER`) — verified by `test_parent_breadcrumb.py::test_breadcrumb_echo_safe`.
